newsitem.title: USA: Neose says ulcer drug results "encouraging".
newsitem.headline: Neose says ulcer drug results "encouraging".

text.p: Neose Technologies Inc on Thursday reported "encouraging" preliminary results of its Phase I safety study with NE-0080, a carbohydrate drug used to detach, and prevent re-attachment of, Helicobacter pylori, the bacterium responsible for most cases of gastritis and ulcers.

The data on the patented, orally administered drug are described in a manuscript that will be presented at the Fourth Annual International Conference on Helicobacter pylori in Washington, D.C., in January, Neose said.
All of the volunteers were H. pylori-positive, but asymptomatic, and received NE-0080 orally for 28 days. The drug was well-tolerated, with no adverse effects reported attributable to the drug.
"As a result of these data, we are continuing to develop NE-0080, and expect to initiate a Phase II trial in patients in early 1997," said Stephen Roth, Neose chief executive, in a statement.
